title: Upstream bug
description: One bug or surprising behaviour that sverify found in a project it builds on (SQLGlot, an engine, Ibis, delta-rs, Substrait's tooling), with enough to file it upstream. Stored as upstream/bugs/<id>.json. Prose fields take a string or a list of paragraphs (Markdown, joined by blank lines).

id.description: Stable id: the project's prefix (SG sqlglot, DF datafusion, DD duckdb, DL deltalake, PL polars, SP spark, IB ibis, ST substrait), a dash, then the next free number. The file is named <id>.json.

version.description: The version the bug was found on (a version or a range).

status.description: unverified: seen, not yet reduced to a minimal repro or checked against the latest upstream release; confirmed: minimal repro on the stated version; filed: reported upstream (the link in upstream); fixed upstream: in the release fixed_in; not a bug: with the reason in status_note.

status_note.description: The status in words: where it reproduces, what is filed or fixed where, or why it is not a bug.

fixed_in.description: The first upstream release with the fix.

upstream.description: Upstream issues, PRs and comments: the report, the fix, related discussion.

repro.description: A minimal reproduction (SQL or Python) with its observed output.

handling.description: How sverify works around it today.

found_by.description: How it was found: the replay, a fuzzer ledger, a probe, a PR or issue.

files.description: Files of this repository that hold the workaround or a test of it, as paths from the repository root.

checked.description: When the entry was last checked, and against which releases.

against.description: Package name to the exact version checked.
